activity: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
knowledge_domain: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
story:
Isla went to the pharmacy with Dad. There was a little sink by the counter. A nurse stood there. She had a bottle of soap with a fox on it.

Isla wanted to open the soap. It was hard to open. The nurse helped her. Then Isla pumped the soap. Bubbles came out on her hands. "Now we sing," said the nurse. They sang a little song about a fox. Isla rubbed and rubbed. The bubbles got big and white. They smelled like flowers.

Then the water washed the bubbles away. Isla's hands were shiny and clean. The nurse clapped. Dad held out a cracker for Isla. Isla looked at her clean hands. She looked at the cracker. Then she took a big bite. Dad smiled. "Yum," said Isla. The fox on the bottle seemed to smile too.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Eli had a library book in his bedroom. It was a book about a big red pot. He wanted to keep it forever.

Eli opened the book. He looked at the first page. He saw little black marks. "Those are words," he said. He pointed at them. He turned the pages one by one, front to back, all the way to the pot picture at the end.

Mama came in. "It is time to take the book back," she said. "It is due today. Other kids want to read it too." Eli held the book tight. "But it is mine," he said. He put it under his pillow. He waited. He waited some more.

Then he heard a frog outside. It went jump, jump, jump. Eli peeked out the window. He saw the frog hop on a leaf.

Eli got the book out from under his pillow. He gave it to Mama. She put it in her bag. "We can borrow it again soon," she said. Eli waved at the book. "Bye, pot," he said.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
story:
Eleanor woke up on her birthday morning. "Today is my day!" she said. Mama was in the kitchen. Grandpa was blowing up balloons. Eleanor watched a balloon get big and round. Then Grandpa let go of the string. The balloon flew up and bumped the ceiling!

Eleanor wanted to make one fly too. She tried to blow a balloon. Puff, puff, puff. It stayed small and flat. "It is too hard," she said. Grandpa smiled. "Watch me take a big, big breath," he said. He puffed and puffed. The balloon grew fat and strong. Then he gave it a tap. Up it went to the ceiling!

"Again!" said Eleanor. Grandpa blew one more. This one had a wheel drawn on it. Eleanor gave it a push. It zoomed up and bounced down. The friends came to the party. They all tapped the balloons up high. Dad lit the cake candles, one by one. Eleanor made a wish and blew them out. The candles went dark. Her breath did that! She grinned and blew at the balloons too. "You cannot blow those down," laughed Grandpa. Eleanor laughed too. "I will pretend I can!" she said, and tapped one way up high.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Leah held her doll and walked into the big store with Mama. "Look how big it is!" said Leah. Her doll was small in her arms. The store doors slid open fast. Then they slid shut slow.

Leah wanted cold milk from the freezer. She touched the glass. "So cold!" she said. "It feels like winter." Then they passed the bakery. Mama pointed. "The oven is hot," she said. "Dad will carry the warm bread." The bread smelled yummy.

At the checkout, a cart went fast. Beep, beep, went the scanner. Then it was their turn. The scanner went slow for their milk. Leah whispered to her doll, "We did it!" Dad put the bread in the bag. Leah took Mama's hand, and they walked out the sliding doors together.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Miles sat at the art table. He wanted to paint a big green frog. But there was no green paint.

He had red paint. He had blue paint. He had yellow paint. No green. "Where is green?" he asked.

His teacher said, "Try mixing two colors."

Miles dipped his brush in blue. He added some yellow. He stirred. Outside, a dog began to bark. Miles looked at his paper. The paint was green!

"Green!" said Miles. "I made green!"

He painted the frog. It was a big green frog. Then he put yellow on top of blue again. More green. He made the frog a green hat, too.

A dot of paint got on his nose. He spun around to show his teacher and felt a little dizzy. She laughed and wiped his nose.

"My frog is green," said Miles. "I made green all by myself."

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Xavier went to the grocery store with Mama. He held his soft bunny in his arms. "Stay close," said Mama.

Then Xavier saw the apples. He picked one up. It was big and red. He put bunny down on a low shelf. He put the apple in the cart.

"Where is bunny?" asked Xavier. Bunny was gone! He looked by the bread. No bunny. He looked by the milk. No bunny.

Mama spoke to a store man. The store man moved a big box of cereal. "Look," he said. "The box was tipped. Bunny slid down, down, down."

There was bunny, under the box! Xavier hugged him. "Bunny, you slid like a slide!"

At lunch time, they shared a snack. Bunny sat right next to Xavier. "No more sliding," said Xavier. Bunny's ears went flop.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Kinsley went to her friend Mia's house. Mia had a big doll named Rosie. Rosie had no blanket. "Rosie is cold," Mia said.

Kinsley wanted to help. She looked around the room. She saw a small red sock on the floor. She put the sock over Rosie's toes. Now Rosie had warm feet. Mia smiled. Then Mia covered Rosie with a play blanket too. "Now Rosie is cozy," said Mia.

The girls played house next. Kinsley set the table with tiny cups. Mia gave each bear a cup. One bear tipped over. Its cup fell on the rug. Kinsley got a cloth. She helped clean the spill. Soon the top of the table was dry and shiny again.

Then the bears got hungry. Mia held a pretend bowl. Kinsley stirred with a pretend spoon. "Time to eat," she said in a big voice. The bears sat very still. After the meal, the bears went to sleep. Kinsley patted them softly, one by one.

"Shh," whispered Mia. "The babies are sleeping." Kinsley tiptoed to the door.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Julia stood in the kitchen next to Grandma. She wanted warm milk, but the milk was cold. "Brrr," said Julia. "My tummy likes it warm."

Grandma poured the milk into a big pot. Julia had a small cup waiting. The pot was big. The cup was small. Grandma put the pot on the stove. "Stay back," said Grandma. "The stove is hot." Julia stood on her step, far away. She watched.

The milk was cold. Then steam came up. Then the milk was warm. Julia saw that hot things made cold things warm. She clapped her hands.

Grandma poured fast, and milk splashed. "Oops," said Grandma. She poured again, slow and careful. The milk went right into the cup. A gray cat ran in. It was fast. It bumped Julia's leg. Julia laughed.

Julia held her warm cup with two hands. It felt good. The cat sat by her feet. "Warm milk for me," said Julia. "And a soft pat for you."

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Nova sat at the big art table. She had red paint and yellow paint. She wanted to paint a green cow for her dream last night. But there was no green paint pot.

Nova looked in the tray. She found blue paint. She looked again. Still no green. Her friend Sam had green, but his pot was almost empty. "You can have a little," Sam said. He poured a tiny drop into her tray. It was not enough.

Nova dipped her brush in yellow. She dipped it in blue. She moved the brush on the paper. The paint turned green! "Look, Sam!" she said. Sam leaned over to see.

Nova painted her green cow under a high blue sky. She painted a big yellow sun. Sam smiled and clapped. Nova made one more green dot and gave it to him.

activity: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
knowledge_domain: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
story:
Charles sat on the big rug at book club. He had a card with the letter B on it. He wanted to find B in his book.

"Is this B?" he asked, pointing to a crooked letter. "No, that is R," said his friend Mia. Charles laughed. R looked like B with one bump missing.

Then his mom said, "B says buh, like bear." Charles looked at his book. He found a big brown animal. "Bear! B!" he said. Mia found a bee. "Bee! B!" she said. They counted the B words. Bear, bee, ball. Three B words!

Charles itched his itchy sweater. His hands were dry from the windy walk. He rubbed them on his knees. Then he pointed at the bear page again.

"Bear starts with B," he said. "One bump, two bumps, B!"

Mia held up a D. "D says duh, like dog," she said. Charles clapped. "I want D next!"

He turned the page to find a dog.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Raphael ran into the doctor's office. He wanted a truck sticker. But first, the doctor had to check him.

"Look at my light," said the doctor. Raphael looked with his eyes. The light was small and bright. He blinked, and the room went dark for a second.

"Now listen," said the doctor. She tapped his knee. Raphael heard the tap with his ears. Then his leg kicked up all by itself! He laughed. "It jumped!" he said.

He smelled the soap on the doctor's hands. He tasted the sweet juice Mom gave him. He touched the soft bed with his fingers.

"You are all done," said the doctor. She held out two stickers. Raphael took the truck one.

"My leg kicked for a sticker too!" he said.

activity: to clap along to the steady beat of a song and sing a nursery rhyme from memory
knowledge_domain: to clap along to the steady beat of a song and sing a nursery rhyme from memory
story:
Kai was in the garage with Dad. Dad turned on the radio. A song came on, bouncy and loud.

"I want to clap," said Kai. He clapped fast, like he was chasing a fly. His claps ran ahead of the song. Then his claps fell behind. His hands got all mixed up.

"Try this," said Dad. Dad patted his knee. Pat, pat, pat. It went the same speed as the song. Kai watched Dad's knee. Then Kai patted his own knee too. Pat, pat, pat. His hands and the song walked together, step by step. "It matches!" said Kai. Dad laughed. "Now try claps." Clap, clap, clap. The claps landed right on the song. Not too fast. Not too slow. Just right.

"Now the words," said Dad. "Twinkle, twinkle, little star." Kai knew some words, but not all. He froze like a statue when the middle part came. Dad sang it slow. Then Dad sang it again. Kai tried once more. "How I wonder what you are!" The words came out, all by themselves, from inside his head.

Kai stood up tall. He clapped and sang at the same time. The radio played. His hands went clap, clap, clap. His voice went up and down. Dad clapped too, silly and big, on purpose too slow just to tease. "Dad, you're too slow!" said Kai. Dad scooped him up in a hug and spun him around. The song kept playing, and Kai kept singing from the middle of the hug. "Like a diamond in the sky!"

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
story:
Amelia woke up and looked out the window. The backyard was white. Snow had come in the night. No school today. It was a snow day at home.

Amelia wanted to make a snowman. She put on her boots and her red coat. Then she went outside. The snow was deep and soft. Her boots sank in. Every step made a hole. Amelia stomped her foot. The snow packed down flat. She stomped again. Now the ground was hard and firm. She could stand right there to build.

Amelia rolled a big ball. It grew bigger and bigger. Then she rolled a small ball for the head. The snowman had a stick arm and a leaf for a hat. "He is so pretty," said Amelia.

Then Amelia saw the bird feeder. It was empty. The birds were cold and hungry. "Wait, birds," she said. Dad came out with a cup of seed. Amelia held out her hand and helped him pour. The birds flew down to eat. Nearby, a small train of ants had gone quiet under the snow, but the birds were here now, and they were happy.

Dad called, "Cocoa time!" Amelia waved to the snowman. "Bye bye. I live here, so I will come back soon." She ran inside, and her boots left little white footprints on the mat.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Mateo was going to the store with Mama. But his little blue dinosaur was gone! "Not my dino," said Mateo. "He rides with me!"

Mateo looked under his seat. No dinosaur. He looked by the door. No dinosaur. "Dino, where are you?" he called.

Mama said, "Look in the back." Mateo turned around. The sun was shining in the window. The sun made his seat shine too. Then something small and shiny rolled out from under the blanket. The sun made it gleam!

"My dino!" shouted Mateo. "The sun made him sparkle! That is how I saw him!" He grabbed his dinosaur and hugged him tight. "You were not alone, dino. The sun was with you."

At the store, Mama said, "They sell toy dinosaurs here too. Do you want a friend for dino?" Mateo held up his dinosaur. "No thank you. This one is my best one."

In the car again, Mateo buckled up. He set the dinosaur on his lap, right in the sun. "See, dino? Now you shine!" The dinosaur gleamed all the way home.

activity: getting a first haircut at a salon
knowledge_domain: getting a first haircut at a salon
story:
Luke went to the mall with his dad. They walked past the toy shop. Luke stopped at a low table. On it was a big red magnet. He picked up the magnet and touched it to some paper clips. The clips jumped up and stuck. "Why do they stick?" he asked. "The magnet picks them up," said Dad.

Then Dad said, "Time for your first haircut." Luke sat in a big chair at the salon. The barber put a cape on him. It felt soft and cool. Then the barber picked up the scissors. Snip, snip. Luke watched the mirror. A piece of his hair fell down. Snip, snip. More hair fell. It slid down the cape and landed on the floor.

"Can the magnet pick up my hair?" Luke asked. The barber smiled and tried. The magnet did not pick up the hair. The hair just lay there. So Luke leaned down and picked up one little piece with his fingers. It was soft and brown. "I will bring this home to show my teddy," he said. The barber put it in a tiny bag and tied it shut. Luke held the bag all the way to the car.

activity: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
knowledge_domain: to hold a pencil correctly and write the letters of their own first name
story:
Ava sat at the big table at writing club. She had a yellow pencil and some paper. She wanted to write her name all by herself.

Ava held the pencil in her whole fist. She pushed hard. The line went bump, bump, bump. It did not look like an A at all. "My letters are wiggly," said Ava. "Like a bee flew over my paper!" said Leo, laughing.

The teacher, Miss Pam, showed Ava how to pinch the pencil near the tip. "Try it like this," she said. Ava pinched the pencil with two fingers. She made a slow line down. Then another line. Then a line across. It was an A! A real A, just sitting there on the paper.

Ava made a V next. Then another A. Ava looked at her letters. Pinch the pencil, and the letters came out neat. Squeeze the pencil, and they wiggled away. She held up her paper. "Look!" she said. "A, V, A! That's me!" Leo clapped. Miss Pam drew a little yellow star next to the A. Ava pinched her pencil again and made one more star of her own.

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
story:
Harper held her mom's hand at the dentist's door. She wanted to be brave. But her tooth felt funny, and she did not know what the dentist would do.

A kind woman in a gray coat said hello. "My name is Doctor Lee," she said. "Let's count your teeth." Harper sat in a big chair. It went up, up, up. Doctor Lee counted out loud. "One tooth, two teeth, three teeth," she said. Harper counted too. She got all the way to twenty.

Then Doctor Lee showed Harper a little tool. "Watch what it does," she said. The tool made water. The water went on a toy tooth. The toy tooth had spots on it. The water washed the spots away. Now the tooth was clean and shiny.

"Will you clean my teeth too?" Harper asked. "Yes," said Doctor Lee. "The water will help." Harper opened her mouth wide, like a little mouse nibbling a cracker. The water tickled a bit. Then it was done. Harper ran to show her mom her clean smile. "Look at my shiny teeth!" she said.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Matteo wanted his red ball. It rolled away at the park. "I will find it," he said.

He used his eyes to look. He saw green grass and a big tree. He used his ears to listen. He heard a bird sing. Then he saw a bucket by the sand. "Maybe my ball is in the bucket," he said.

He used his nose to smell. He smelled flowers, not his ball. He walked on. "Use your eyes, use your ears," said Mama. She held his hand. "Be careful near the water."

Then Matteo touched the bucket with his fingers. The sand felt warm and soft. His ball was not there. Then Mama opened her bag. She took out a snack. Matteo tasted an apple. It was sweet.

A boy came by. "Is this red ball yours?" he asked. "Yes! Thank you!" said Matteo. He gave the boy a big hug.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story:
Levi ran to the art table at school. He wanted to build a house for his toy animal. Miss Maya gave him paper shapes. There was a round circle. There was a boxy square. There were three more shapes too.

Levi tried the circle for the roof. It rolled right off! He laughed and chased it. The circle would not stay on top. Then he tried a triangle. It had three pointy sides. It sat still on the square. The roof stayed up!

Levi picked two rectangles. He pressed them on for walls. The square became the floor. His toy animal went inside. "A house!" Levi shouted. Miss Maya clapped. Levi put the circle on top of the roof, like a moon. "Look at my new house!" he said.

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Elizabeth went to the park with her dad. She saw the big slide. She wanted to slide down fast.

Elizabeth put her hand on the slide. The slide was very hot. She pulled her hand back quick. "Ouch," she said. The sun had made the slide hot. Her dad felt it too. "Let's find a shady slide," he said.

They found a little slide under a tree. Elizabeth touched it. This one was cool. She climbed up and slid down. Slip, slip, slip. She laughed and did it again.

Then she saw the grill by the picnic table. Smoke came out of it. It looked big and warm. Was it hot like the slide? Elizabeth began to walk over. Her dad took her gentle hand. "The grill is very hot," he said. "Daddy touches it. Not you." Elizabeth stayed with her dad and watched from far away.

The hot dog was ready. Her dad gave her a cool one on a plate. Elizabeth held her dad's hand all the way to the bench. "I sit close to you," she said. Her dad smiled. "Yes, you do."

activity: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
knowledge_domain: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
story:
Thomas put his arms in his coat. He pulled the zipper up, up, up. But the zipper stopped. It would not move.

The store was cold by the freezer. Thomas shivered. He wanted his coat zipped all the way. He tugged again. The zipper still stuck.

Daddy knelt down. "Look at the bottom," he said. Thomas looked. The two sides were apart. He pushed them together. The little metal part clicked into place. Then Thomas pulled the zipper up. It went all the way to his chin! "Neat!" said Thomas. He put his hand on his chest. The coat was snug.

They walked to the fruit. There was a long line at the apples. Thomas got to put four apples in the bag. Then he wanted to try again. He unzipped his coat all by himself. He lined up the bottom. Click. Up went the zipper.

On the walk to the car, Thomas zipped and unzipped. "I did it," he said. "All by me."

activity: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
knowledge_domain: basic social rules such as turn-taking, sharing, fairness and following simple group rules
story:
Avery went to the store with Dad. She wanted a red apple. But when they got to the fruit bin, there was one apple left. A boy was already standing there. He reached for the apple too.

"You go first," said the boy. He held out the apple. "Then I can pick a pear." Avery took the apple. "Thank you," she said. The boy smiled and took a green pear.

At the bread counter, there was a long line. Avery asked Dad, "Why do we stand in line?" Dad said, "So everyone gets bread in turn." Avery watched. One lady went, then a man, then a girl. Each person got bread, one by one. Soon it was Dad's turn, and he got a warm loaf.

The checkout lady's phone rang. She answered it, then put it down. "Now I can help you," she said. Avery put the apple on the belt. The scanner beeped, and the numbers danced on the screen. Dad paid with coins. He gave Avery one small coin to hold.

Outside, Dad cut the apple with a sharp knife, safely at the picnic table. He gave half to Avery and half to the boy, who was sitting there too. "Half and half," said Dad. Avery bit her piece. It was sweet and crunchy. "We both got some," she said. The boy raised his pear like a toast. "To apples and pears," he said.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
story:
Jacob sat in the big chair at the doctor's office. He wanted a sticker, but first the doctor had to check him. "Open your eyes wide," said Dr. Ana. Jacob saw a little light. "Good. Your eyes see the light," she said.

Then she took out a tiny hammer. Tap, tap, it went on his knee. His leg jumped up all by itself. Jacob laughed. "My leg moved!" he said.

"Yes, your knee sent a message," said Dr. Ana. She tapped again. Tap. Up went his leg again.

Next she held a cup near his nose. Jacob sniffed it with his nose. "Orange!" he said. She gave him a sweet candy for his tongue. Then she whispered, "Can you hear me?" Jacob's ears heard the soft words.

There was a fish tank in the corner. The blue water looked like a little river. "I remember that tank," Jacob said. Dr. Ana smiled. "Your voice was weak last time. Now it is strong."

She tapped his knee one more time. Up it went, and she handed him a shiny dinosaur sticker.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Aubrey sat on the red rug at daycare. Miss Jo held up a big bag. "These books are from the library," she said. "We can take them home. But we bring them back on Friday, so other kids can read them too." Max grabbed the dinosaur book. "This one is mine forever," he said. He hugged it tight.

Aubrey peeked at a book about a little duck. She opened it. "Miss Jo, what does this say?" Miss Jo pointed at the words. "Those letters say, 'Duck goes for a swim.'" Aubrey gasped. The marks on the page were words. Words that Miss Jo could say out loud. Aubrey turned one page, then the next. She started at the front and went to the back, just like Miss Jo showed.

Then Max began to cry. "I want to keep it forever," he said. Aubrey had a question. She thought hard. "Miss Jo, can Max take it home and bring it back on Friday?" Miss Jo smiled. "Yes, that is how it works. Then it comes back for Aubrey." Max wiped his eyes. "You can have it after me," he said. Aubrey clapped. "And then it comes back for you again," she said. Max held out the book so they could both peek at the very first page together.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Ella wanted to play house at daycare. But Ben had the baby doll. Ella said, "Can I hold her?" Ben shook his head. Ella felt sad.

Then the baby doll fell on the floor. "Ow," said Ben. A little scratch showed on the doll's arm. "Oh no," said Ella. "Is she hurt?" Teacher Mia came over. "She needs a bandage," she said. She put glue on a paper bandage and stuck it on. "There. Now she needs a mama."

Ben looked at Ella. "You can be the mama," he said. Ella took the doll. She wrapped her in a soft blanket. The doll stopped crying right away.

"Shh," said Ella. "Sleep now." She patted the blanket. "Sorry you fell." Teacher Mia smiled and sat close by. The baby slept, and Ella rocked her, very gentle, very slow.

activity: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
knowledge_domain: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
story:
Nora looked out the big window. "It is sunny today!" she said. The sun made bright spots on the floor. Nora put on her orange hat. Off she went to paint a picture of her toy turtle in the sun.

Then the sky got dark. Drip, drop, drip. "Oh no, it is rainy!" said Nora. The rain wet her picture. Mommy gave her boots and a rain coat. Splash, splash went the puddles.

Then the wind began to whoosh. "It is windy!" said Nora. The wind blew her orange hat away. Daddy ran fast and caught it. "My hat!" said Nora. She hugged it tight.

Then white flakes fell down. "It is snowy!" said Nora. Mommy helped her put on mittens and a warm coat. Nora made a little snow turtle. It was sunny again. Nora clapped her hands and said, "Look, look, look what I made!"

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
story:
Isaiah sat on the rug in the living room. The big game was on TV. Grandma sat beside him. Uncle Max and Cousin Mia were there too. Everyone was shouting and clapping.

Isaiah wanted to see better. The big chair was in his way. He tried to peek around it. He could only see half the TV. "I can't see the game," he said.

Then Isaiah saw Grandma wave a big fan. The fan made air move. The air made the curtain spin and puff out wide. When the curtain puffed, the TV showed through the gap! Isaiah tugged Grandma's sleeve. He pointed at the curtain. Grandma smiled and held the fan steady. The curtain stayed wide open. Isaiah saw the whole game.

The team scored. Everyone jumped up. Isaiah clapped so hard his tooth pinged, the loose one. "We won!" he shouted. Grandma pulled him onto her lap for a big hug.

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
story:
Max was at Grandma's house. Grandma had a jar of honey and a big orange. Max wanted to taste the honey. Grandma put a little honey on a spoon. Max licked it. "Yum!" he said. "My tongue did that!"

Grandma cut the orange. It smelled sweet. Max put his nose close. "My nose smells it!" he said. Then he heard a bird at the window. "My ears hear the bird!" Max tapped his toes. "My feet can hear too?"

Grandma laughed. "Try this," she said. She held up a soft, red mitten. Max touched it. "My hands feel it. It is soft." Then Grandma pointed at the mitten. "What do you see?" Max looked. "My eyes see red! I did not miss it!"

"Now close your eyes," said Grandma. Max closed them tight. He was brave in the dark. "Can you see the mitten?" she asked. "No," said Max. "My eyes are sleeping." Then the bird sang again. Max smiled. "But my ears still work!"

Grandma hugged him. "Five helpers," she said. Max counted on his fingers. Then he touched the mitten one more time, just to be sure.

activity: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
knowledge_domain: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
story:
Ivy held a small box on the walk home. Inside was her new goldfish. He was small and orange. His name was Pip.

At home, Dad put water in a bowl. "Pip needs food too," Dad said. "Just a little pinch."

Ivy opened the food can. She took a big handful with her hand. Dad shook his head. "Too much," he said. "A little pinch, like snow flakes falling."

Ivy put back most of the food. She pinched two little flakes. She dropped them in the bowl. The flakes sat on top of the water.

Then Ivy saw it. Pip swam up, up, up. He opened his tiny mouth. He ate a flake. He ate the other one too.

"Look, Dad! He likes it!" Ivy said.

The old bowl still had spots on the glass. "It looks ugly," said Ivy. Dad wiped it with a cloth. Now it was shiny and clear.

Ivy fed Pip one pinch every day. Each time, up he came, mouth open wide.

"Hello, Pip," said Ivy.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story:
Arya sat on the big red rug at the library. Miss Jo sang the counting song. "One, two, three," she sang. Arya loved that song. But the numbers ran away from her after three.

Arya wanted to sing the whole song. "Four, um, six?" she said. The boy next to her giggled. "Not quite," he said kindly.

Miss Jo had an idea. "Count my books," she said. She put a book in Arya's hands. Arya patted it. "One!" Another book came. "Two!" Miss Jo kept handing her books. Pat, say. Pat, say. "Three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!"

Arya looked at the tall stack. Ten books! The top book wobbled. Arya held it steady.

Then she sang the whole song all by herself. "One to ten!" she shouted.

"Shh," said the boy, giggling. He clapped very quietly.

Miss Jo gave Arya a small salty cracker. "My best counter," she said.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
story:
Rosalie stood by the pool with her swim team. The water was blue and cool. Her coach pointed to a big red ball. It sat flat on the water, floating like a boat.

"Can you move the ball without touching it?" asked Coach Ben. Rosalie tipped her head. "How?" she wondered. Coach Ben smiled. "Try kicking your feet in the water."

Rosalie sat on the edge. She splashed her feet. Small waves went out. The red ball bobbed. She kicked faster. Bigger waves rolled across the pool. The ball began to move! It drifted all the way to the ladder.

"I did it!" Rosalie shouted. "My feet made waves. The waves pushed the ball!" The other kids clapped for her. Then they all sat down and kicked too. Soon the whole pool was full of rolling waves, and the red ball danced across the water.

activity: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
knowledge_domain: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
story:
Ali stood in the backyard. Mama sat in the big chair with a bundle in her arms. "This is your baby sister," Mama said. Ali looked at the tiny face. "She is so small," he said.

The baby began to cry. Ali felt sad. "She is crying," he said. Then he saw his red ball on the grass. He rolled it gently to the baby's feet. The baby stopped crying. She watched the ball. Ali rolled it again. She made a small sound, like a laugh.

"You did not lose your spot, Ali," said Papa. "You are still our big boy." Ali picked up his last toy from the sandbox. He put it by the baby's blanket. "This is for you," he said. The baby grabbed his finger and held on tight.

activity: getting a first haircut at a salon
knowledge_domain: getting a first haircut at a salon
story:
Anthony sat in the car with Mom. They were going to meet a hair cutter. "Will she use scissors?" Anthony asked. "Yes, the small kind," said Mom. Anthony touched his long hair. He liked his hair.

At the salon, a lady put a cape on Anthony. It was blue and shiny. Then she picked up her scissors. Snip, snip, snip. Anthony watched in the big mirror. Each time the scissors closed, a piece of hair fell down. Snip, then a piece fell. Snip, and another piece fell. Soon little hairs lay all over the floor, like soft brown snow.

Then came the surprise. Anthony looked in the mirror. His hair was short now. His ears were showing. Back in the car, Mom flipped down the sun visor. Anthony looked in the little mirror there too. "That's me!" he said. He turned his head one way, then the other. The boy in the mirror turned too. Anthony smiled at him. The boy smiled back.

activity: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
knowledge_domain: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
story: Riley went to the vet with her dad. There were pets in little rooms. A dog barked. A rabbit ate a leaf. One tank held a long, quiet snake. Riley looked and looked. Then she saw a small orange fish. Its water was cloudy. The fish sat very still. "I want this one," said Riley. The vet smiled. "Then we must help him feel better." Dad poured out the cloudy water. He poured in clean water. Riley watched and waited. The water turned clear. Then the fish swam all around. It wiggled its little tail. At home, Riley sorted her new things. The food went in one cup. The shells went in a row. Each morning she dropped one tiny bit of food in the tank. The fish swam up fast and ate it. "Hello, little fish," said Riley. The fish blew a bubble.

activity: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
knowledge_domain: opposite pairs such as big and small, hot and cold, fast and slow
story:
Elena wanted to draw a duck at the park. But the duck kept swimming away. The duck was fast. Elena could not see it well.

A big duck came near. It was very big. Then a small duck came too. It was very small. The small duck sat on the water and stayed still. Now Elena could see a duck that did not move.

The sun felt hot on her head. Mommy gave her a cold drink. "Ahh," said Elena. The cold drink felt good. She took a big sip and picked up her crayon.

The small duck stayed slow and still. Elena drew it, slow and careful. She drew its small head. She drew its small tail. Then she wrote her name on the paper.

"My new drawing!" said Elena. Mommy clapped. Elena held it up to the pond. The small duck swam by, slow as can be. "Look, duck," said Elena. "That is you."

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Jasmine ran to the sandbox with her bear. She set bear on a big rock. "You sit here, baby," she said. But bear kept tipping over. He fell into the sand again.

Jasmine wanted bear to sit like a grown-up. She looked around. Then she dug a small hole in the sand. She pushed bear's bottom into the hole. The sand held him up. Bear sat tall and still!

"Time to cook," said Jasmine. She found two cups and a spoon. She put sand in one cup. She put sand in the other. She mixed them with the spoon. "Soup for my baby," she sang.

A boy named Sam came by. "Can I play?" he asked. "Yes," said Jasmine. "You can be the dad." Sam picked up a leaf. "I will cook a leaf pie," he said.

Then bear tipped forward. His nose went right into the soup cup. "Oh no, baby is hungry!" Jasmine laughed. She lifted him up and patted his back. She held the warm cup to his snout. Sam waved a friendly hand at bear.

"More soup," said Sam. "Coming right up."

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Declan wanted to wash his hands all by himself. He stood by the sink and looked at the shiny tap. "Can I do it?" he asked. Mama smiled and stood close behind him.

Mama turned the red tap a tiny bit. The water came out. Declan put one finger near it. "Ooh, warm," he said. He pulled his hand back fast. Warm water could feel too hot. So Mama turned the blue tap instead. Now the water ran cool and soft. Declan let it run over his fingers. "Cold feels nice," he said. He rubbed the soap into white bubbles. The bubbles smelled like paint, fresh and clean. He blew one bubble off his thumb. It popped in the air.

Next to the sink sat a little pink bottle. Declan reached for it. Mama's hand came down quick and soft. "That one is for grown-ups," she said. Declan put his hand back in the water. The tap turned off. The water stopped. Declan turned it on again. The water ran. He turned it off. The water stopped. His tap, his water, his trick.

"You did the whole wash," said Mama. Declan looked at his hands. They were shiny and clean. Then he saw something small in the mirror. A shy little smile, and it was his own.

activity: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
knowledge_domain: basic shape concepts such as circle, square, triangle and rectangle
story:
Emile had a small toy bear at daycare. He wanted to build the bear a house. "A house needs a door," said Emile.

He found a round block. He put it by the wall. The round block rolled away. "Come back, circle," said Emile.

He tried a block with three sides. It stood still, but it was too small for the door. The bear could not fit through.

Then Emile found a block with four flat sides. Two sides were long, and two sides were short. It stood like a door. "Hello, rectangle," said Emile.

He set the rectangle in the wall. The bear went in. The bear came out. "You can go in and out," said Emile.

Outside, his shoe tapped the floor. He looked at the window and saw cold rain. That was fine. The bear was dry inside.

Emile put a triangle on top. "Now it has a roof," he said. "I wish I could fit in there too."

activity: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
knowledge_domain: simple safety concepts such as hot versus cold, staying close to caregivers and not touching dangerous objects
story:
Billie ran to the playground with her grandma. The sun made the slide very hot. Billie put her hand near it. The slide felt hot like her soup at lunch. She pulled her hand back.

Grandma poured cool water on the slide. Billie watched the water run down. She touched the slide again. Now it was cool. The water had made it cool. Billie went down the slide. "Whee!" she said.

Then Billie saw something shiny in the sand. It was a broken bottle. She wanted to pick it up. "Stop," said grandma. "That can cut you." Grandma picked it up with a bag. She put it in the bin. Billie threw away some paper she found. They sorted the trash together.

A big dog ran by. Billie held grandma's hand. The dog sniffed them and trotted off. Billie and grandma sat on the bench. "The sun makes things hot," said Billie. Grandma smiled. Billie pointed at the shady tree. "That spot is not hot." They sat in the shade and ate their crackers.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story: Matteo was in the car seat. He wanted to see ten trucks before the farm. "Look, one truck!" said Mama. "One!" said Matteo. The truck went past the window. Then two cars went by. "Two cars!" said Matteo. He clapped his hands. Mama honked the horn. A big old bus beeped back. "Beep, beep!" laughed Matteo. Three cows stood by the fence. Then four birds flew over the road. "This is the best car ride," said Matteo. Five, six, seven cars went by in a line. "I count them!" he said. Eight bikes rang their bells. Then came a big red truck. "Nine!" said Mama. Matteo leaned forward. One more truck came around the bend. "Ten!" he shouted. "I did it! I saw ten!" Matteo could not wait to tell his teacher all about it.
